summary: Governor of Pennsylvania 1951–55, born in a mine patch at Alden in Newport Township; Luzerne County judge and Superior Court judge; John's 5th cousin 2 times removed.
bio:
John Sydney Fine was born on 10 April 1893 in a mine-patch house at Alden, Newport Township, Luzerne County, the son of Jacob W. Fine, a coal miner, and Margaret Croop. Through his mother he descended from Philip Croup, the Palatine settler of Newport Township and a brother of John's ancestor Frederick Croup, which makes him John's fifth cousin twice removed. The family moved to Nanticoke, where he went to high school, and he took his law degree at Dickinson in 1914, joined the Luzerne County bar in 1915 and studied at Trinity College, Dublin, in 1919 while stationed in Ireland.

He rose through Luzerne County Republican politics, serving as county chairman in 1922–23, and in 1927 Governor Gifford Pinchot appointed him to the Court of Common Pleas, where voters kept him for twenty years. Governor James Duff named him to the Superior Court in 1947, and in 1950 he left the bench to run for governor. He served from January 1951 to January 1955. He married Helene Pennebecker Morgan in 1939; she died in April 1951, three months into his term, leaving two sons. In later years he farmed at Loyalville in Luzerne County. He died on 21 May 1978 and was buried in Oak Lawn Cemetery, Nanticoke.
notable: Governor of Pennsylvania, 1951–1955; judge of the Luzerne County Court of Common Pleas 1927–47 and of the Pennsylvania Superior Court 1947–50.
